## Overview
Azure Cosmos DB (NoSQL API) implementation for the Birko data layer providing document-based storage with transactional batch support.

## Project Location
`Birko.Data.CosmosDB/`

## Purpose
- Document-based storage via Azure Cosmos DB NoSQL API
- Transactional batch operations (scoped to partition key)
- LINQ-based queries via Microsoft.Azure.Cosmos SDK v3
- Bulk execution for high-throughput scenarios

## Components

### Stores
- `CosmosDBStore<T>` - Synchronous Cosmos DB store
- `AsyncCosmosDBStore<T>` - Asynchronous Cosmos DB store with transactional batch support
- `CosmosFilterRewrite` - the one filter pre-pass of both stores and the view store (TASK-896, see below)
- `CosmosDateTimeOrder` - corrects a read sorted by a DateTime member to C#'s order, for both stores and the view store (TASK-902)
- **A long `Contains` list (TASK-834).** The SDK writes the list into the query text, so past 524,288 characters
  (13,105 Guids, measured) Cosmos DB answers 400 SC3020.
  - **Split, by `CosmosInListChunking`:** reads, counts, and filtered updates and deletes, sync and async, in chunks of
    at most `InListChunkSize` (1000) values. The split applies only when the list is a plain AND conjunct of scalar
    values or strings with no sort or paging.
  - **Cut by length too (TASK-842).** A chunk also ends where its query text would pass the limit less a margin of a
    sixteenth (32,768 characters), and each chunk is measured with the store's own rendering and halved until it fits.
    So 1,200 strings of 600 characters, which one 1,000-value chunk overflows, are read; a list under 1,000 values is
    split when its query is over that budget. The server counts characters, not UTF-8 bytes (measured on the
    emulator). A single value whose query alone is over the limit is refused by name (`one value ...`), never sent.
  - **Strings split here, not on SQL.** Cosmos DB has no collation: `IN` and `ARRAY_CONTAINS` match only the
    ordinally equal string (case, a trailing space, U+00E9 vs `e`+U+0301 each measured distinct on the emulator,
    TASK-841), so distinct strings make disjoint chunks. The SQL `InListChunkPlanner` refuses strings (TASK-833: a
    case- or accent-insensitive collation can make two strings one value).
  - **Refused:** any other shape past the limit gets `NotSupportedException` before any request.
  - **Writes are not atomic across chunks.** A failure at chunk 2 or later throws `CosmosChunkedWriteException`
    naming the chunks applied. `CosmosViewStore` reads and counts go through the same planner (TASK-839).

### Repositories
- `CosmosDBRepository<TViewModel, TModel>` - ViewModel repository
- `AsyncCosmosDBRepository<TViewModel, TModel>` - Async ViewModel repository
- `CosmosDBModelRepository<T>` - Direct model repository
- `AsyncCosmosDBModelRepository<T>` - Async direct model repository

### UnitOfWork
- `CosmosDbUnitOfWork` - Wraps `TransactionalBatch` (partition-key scoped)
  - The batch is spent once sent: a refused batch is a `UnitOfWorkException` naming the status, a thrown one propagates unchanged, and the rollback after a failed commit is a no-op (TASK-578)

### IndexManagement
- `CosmosDBIndexManager` - Manages indexing policies (included paths, composite indexes, spatial indexes). Index names are kept in the `__birko_indexes` registry container (TASK-628); `Unique`, `Sparse`, `ExpireAfter`, non-standard field types, a single descending field and `Properties` are refused

## Connection

### Settings (Birko.Data.CosmosDB.Stores.Settings)
Typed settings class extending `RemoteSettings`:
- `PartitionKeyPath` (default: "/id"): **only `/id` is supported**, and any other value throws `NotSupportedException`
  when settings are applied (TASK-614). Every point operation passes `new PartitionKey(guid)`. Supporting another path
  would mean deriving the value from the entity, and a read or delete by Guid could no longer name its partition. An
  existing container on another path is already refused by the SDK at init (measured).
- `RequestTimeout` (default: 30 seconds) — request timeout
- `AllowBulkExecution` (default: true) — enables bulk execution mode
- `GetCosmosClientOptions()` — builds `CosmosClientOptions` from settings

Settings mapping from `RemoteSettings`:
- `Location` = connection string or endpoint URL
- `Name` = database name
- `Password` = account key (when using endpoint URL)
- `UserName` = container name (optional, defaults to type name)

### Legacy Settings (still supported)
`SetSettings(ISettings)` accepts `Birko.Configuration.RemoteSettings` and wraps it into a `Settings` instance with defaults.

## Dependencies
- Birko.Data.Core
- Birko.Data.Stores
- Birko.Data.Patterns (UnitOfWork, IndexManagement)
- Microsoft.Azure.Cosmos v3.46.1

## Important Notes
- Transactional batches are scoped to a single partition key
- The partition key path is "/id"; `Settings.PartitionKeyPath` accepts nothing else (TASK-614)
- Bulk execution is enabled by default via `Settings.AllowBulkExecution = true`
- Sync store operations use `.GetAwaiter().GetResult()` wrappers; prefer async store for production

## Filters answer null and missing members as C# does (TASK-896)
Every filter, on every path (reads sync and async, counts, the read behind `Update(filter, …)` / `Delete(filter)`,
aggregates) and in the view store, takes ONE pre-pass: `CosmosFilterRewrite.Prepare` = `SpanContains`,
`DateTruncation`, `NullOrderingFold`, `NullSemantics`, then `DateTimeKeys` (TASK-902). Add a rewrite there, never at a call site.
- **Measured before** (emulator, vnext-preview, 2026-11-10; 93 shapes over nullable members, 2 of 10 documents
  omitting them): 53 shapes silently answered other rows than the compiled expression and 14 threw the SDK's
  `DocumentQueryException`, identically on all 7 paths.
  `x.Score.HasValue` rendered `IS_DEFINED`, true of a stored null (8 rows where C# has 5); `!(x.Score > 20)` missed the
  null rows (an ordering with null is undefined in Cosmos DB, and so is its NOT); every `== null`, `!=`, `IN (.., null)`,
  `NOT IN` and negated equality skipped a document that omits the member (undefined under every operator, while C#
  reads it as null); `x.Flag ?? false` kept a stored null (`??` replaces only undefined); `string.Compare` /
  `CompareTo` rendered Cosmos DB's ordinal order for C#'s culture order (`"C7"` vs `"c2"` the other way round);
  `IsNullOrEmpty`, `IsNullOrWhiteSpace`, `GetValueOrDefault`, `CompareOrdinal` and the ordinal `Compare` were the throws.
- **The rewrite.** "Has a value" is `IS_DEFINED(x) AND NOT IS_NULL(x)`, "null" is `NOT IS_DEFINED(x) OR IS_NULL(x)`
  (both always true or false). `HasValue`, `== null`, `!= null`, `!=` (a guarded equality, negated), two nullable
  operands compared for equality, a list holding `null`, `??` and `GetValueOrDefault` (a conditional on "has a value")
  are rewritten everywhere. A comparison under an odd number of `!`, or anywhere but `&&` / `||` / `!`, is guarded with
  "has a value"; a positive one keeps its rendering (an undefined row is simply not returned), so ordinary filters
  render as before.
- **Strings.** `IsNullOrEmpty` translates. `CompareOrdinal(m, v)` and `Compare(m, v, StringComparison.Ordinal)` against
  0 render `m op v` with null first. **Refused by name** (`NotSupportedException` naming TASK-896, before any request):
  `IsNullOrWhiteSpace` (Cosmos DB's TRIM keeps U+00A0, U+0085, U+001C, measured), every culture or ignore-case
  comparison (`Compare(a, b)`, `CompareTo`, `Compare(.., true)`, `OrdinalIgnoreCase`, culture overloads), an ordinal
  one whose value holds a character at or above U+D800 (Cosmos DB orders by code point, .NET by UTF-16 unit: U+1F600
  sorts after U+FFFF, measured), two members compared, a computed member, a result compared with anything but 0.
- **After:** 0 of the 91 translated shapes differ, on every path; the 12 refused shapes refuse on every path and a
  refused write changes no row (`Task896NullSemanticsLiveTests`).
- The rewritten tree is never compiled; a second pass (a chunked write prepares each chunk again) only repeats guards,
  and leaves the `IS_DEFINED` / `IS_NULL` markers and a defaulted read it produced alone.

## Missing non-nullable members, nested predicates, lists holding null (TASK-899)
- **A non-nullable member a document omits** (written before the member existed) is the type's default to every
  reader and undefined to Cosmos DB. Measured on the emulator (vnext-preview, 2026-11-10; 44 shapes, 2 of 7 documents
  omitting `int`, `bool`, enum, `DateTime`, `decimal`, `double`, `long` members): 34 answered other rows, identically on
  all 7 paths (`x.A == 0`, `x.A != 5`, `!(x.A > 3)`, `!x.Del`, `x.Del == false`, `x.E == New`, `ids.Contains(x.A)` with 0,
  `x.A > x.Score`, `x.A + 1 == 1` all skipped those documents). Now (`IsDefaultable`: a value-type member read along
  members of document classes from a lambda parameter, not `Nullable.Value`, not a struct's or string's member):
  - against a value, `m op v` where the default passes it is `NOT IS_DEFINED(m) OR m op v`; where it fails, it keeps its
    rendering (and its index), guarded with `IS_DEFINED(m)` under `!`. A `Contains` of `m` likewise. A bare `bool`
    member under `!` is `IS_DEFINED(m) AND m`.
  - in anything computed (`m + 1`, `m > x.Other`, a conditional) the member is `IS_DEFINED(m) ? m : default`.
  - Not covered: a member stored as JSON `null` on a non-nullable type, which no reader can read; a missing parent
    object (`x.Sub.A` without `Sub`), where C# throws.
- **Nested predicates** (`Any`, `Where`, `Count`, `First`, … over an array) take the same rewrite, their body positive
  whatever the polarity outside (an element whose test is undefined is simply not kept, C#'s false). **`All(p)` is
  `!Any(!p)`**: the provider has no `All` and threw `DocumentQueryException` on every path. Measured before: 23 of 30
  shapes wrong on reads, counts and writes: 10 `All` shapes threw, 13 `Any` / `Count` / `Where` shapes answered other rows
  (`Any(i => i.S == null)`, `Any(i => !(i.Score > 5))`, `Any(i => i.N == 0)` skipped null and missing members). After: 0 on reads, counts, update and delete. **An aggregate whose filter holds one is refused by
  name** (TASK-876's message): the provider renders a nested predicate as a `JOIN (SELECT VALUE EXISTS(...))`, not a
  plain `WHERE` the aggregation can be placed behind.
- **A list holding `null`, or a non-nullable member's default, splits past the limit.** TASK-896 rendered it
  `absent OR IN (..)`, which the planner refused past 524,288 characters as "under an OR" (measured: 30,000 names with
  a null, 100,000 ints with 0). `CosmosFilterRewrite.TryAbsentOrIn` recognises the shape it produced, and
  `CosmosInListChunking` splits the IN with the absent leg in ONE chunk: no stored value of the list matches a null or
  missing member, so the chunks stay disjoint. For a default, the chunk holding the default carries it (re-preparing a
  chunk, as a chunked write does, adds the leg to that chunk). Negated (`!list.Contains(..)` with null) it is still
  refused past the limit. `Task899AbsentLegChunkingLiveTests`.
- **Query cost of `IS_DEFINED` / `IS_NULL`: unmeasured.** The emulator charges 1 RU per page whatever the query and
  returns no index metrics (`PopulateIndexMetrics`; measured 2026-11-10 on 4,000 documents, also for
  `(IS_DEFINED(c.A) ? c.A : 0) = 5`), so it cannot show index use. A test the default fails keeps its plain, indexable
  rendering; the `NOT IS_DEFINED(m) OR ..` leg and a defaulted computed operand are what a real account would have to
  be measured for.

## DateTime filters and sorts answer as C# (TASK-902)
- **How a DateTime is stored.** Birko's serializer (System.Text.Json defaults) writes ISO 8601 text with as many
  fraction digits as the value needs, none for a whole second (`…10:00:00`, `…10:00:00.5`, `…10:00:00.0000001`), then
  `Z` for UTC, the writer's offset for local (`+01:00`, `+02:00` in summer), nothing for unspecified. It reads `Z` back
  as UTC, an offset as the reader's local time (converted), no suffix as unspecified. The LINQ provider renders a caller's
  value in the same form. C# compares two DateTimes by their ticks, whatever the kind; Cosmos DB compared and sorted the
  text, so within one second the order was `"…00"`, `"…00+01:00"`, `"…00.0000001Z"`, `"…00.5Z"`, `"…00Z"`, and an
  equality held only between equal texts (a local and a UTC time of one wall clock were unequal).
- **Measured before** (emulator, vnext-preview, 2026-11-10; 12 documents of every kind and fraction, two omitting
  members; `Task902DateTimeLiveTests`): 76 of 88 filter shapes answered other rows than C# on some path (reads 73,
  counts and the aggregate WHERE 70, update and delete 76, sync and async alike; 6 of them threw `DocumentQueryException`:
  `Equals`, `Compare`, `CompareTo`, `AddDays`). A sort answered another order on 62 of 120 sorted reads (5 sorts x 2
  filters x 12 pages), sync and async. After: 0, and the 9 refused shapes refuse on every path.
- **Filters (`CosmosFilterRewrite.DateTimeKeys`, the last step of `Prepare`, so store, view, counts, writes and the
  aggregate WHERE share it).** Every comparison of a stored DateTime compares a wall-clock key: the first 19 characters
  (the wall clock to the second, in every stored form) and the fraction, padded to 7 digits. A caller's value is keyed in
  C# from its ticks, so its kind does not matter, as in C#. Against a value the key is preceded by a plain text range on
  the member (`m >= "…10:00:00"` of the value's second, `m < "…10:00:01"`), which holds every row the key matches, so
  the range index can narrow the rows (not measurable on the emulator, which reports no index metrics). Translated too:
  member against member, a `Contains` list (a list of keys, split past the query limit like any other), `.Date`
  against another member's `.Date`, `Equals`, `DateTime.Compare(a, b)` / `a.CompareTo(b)` against 0 (the provider threw
  for these three). Null and missing members keep TASK-896/899's semantics.
- **Sorts (`CosmosDateTimeOrder`).** Cosmos DB sorts only by a document path, so the server's text order is kept and
  corrected: it is C#'s at the second, so only rows that share a second (and every earlier sort key) can be out of
  order, and those runs are sorted in memory by ticks. On a paged read, a run that crosses the page's edge is read whole
  (a second query: the filter AND the run's keys) and the page takes the run's rows at the positions it covered; where
  one run covers the whole page, the rows after it are read too (at most the run's size). A sort with no DateTime key is
  untouched. Both stores and the view store.
- **Exact when** a value stored with an offset was written with the reader's offset, as TASK-897's aggregates and the
  time bucket already assume: such a value reads back converted to the reader's local time.
- **Refused by name** (`NotSupportedException` naming TASK-902, before any request; a refused write changes no row):
  - a comparison, a list or a sort of a `DateTimeOffset` member: C# compares the instant, the stored text holds the
    writer's offset, and the provider renders no conversion (measured: `O == o` missed the same instant written with
    another offset, `O > o` matched an earlier one);
  - a member of a stored DateTime (`Year`, `Hour`, `Ticks`, `TimeOfDay`, ...): the provider rendered `root["T"]["Year"]`,
    a property of a string, and matched nothing (measured);
  - a DateTime computed from a member (`x.T.AddDays(1)`; the provider threw `DocumentQueryException`), a `Compare` result
    against anything but 0.
- **Write-side option, not taken.** Writing a fixed-width form (always 7 digits and `Z`) would make plain text
  comparisons exact and indexable for new documents, but existing documents keep their text, so the read-side key is
  needed anyway until a migration rewrites them; and it would change what every other reader of the container sees.
  Cosmos DB's computed properties (an indexed `cp_t` holding the key, sortable) would make both sorts and filters
  index-served, but need a container-definition change, and the emulator accepts the definition and then answers nothing
  for it (measured), so it cannot be tested here.

## Aggregation (TASK-876)
- `Aggregate` / `AggregateAsync` run one native query: `SELECT … FROM root [WHERE …] [GROUP BY …]`.
- **The WHERE is the reads' rendering.** The filter gets the reads' pre-pass (`CosmosFilterRewrite.Prepare`, above),
  then goes through `BuildQuery(...).ToQueryDefinition()`. `CosmosAggregationHelper.BuildAggregateQuery`
  takes the predicate from that text with its parameters, so the aggregate is written over the LINQ alias `root`.
  A rendering that is not `SELECT VALUE root FROM root WHERE …` is refused by name, never dropped.
- **Before:** `BuildAggregateSql` (removed) emitted no WHERE, so every filter was ignored, silently. Measured on the
  emulator: `A > 3` counted 6 of 6, and all 22 filtered cases (11 shapes, grouped and not) were wrong.
- **IN lists:** groups cannot be merged across chunks, so an aggregate is one query. Past the ceiling it is refused
  before any request, as a sorted read is.
- **Lazy init:** an aggregate initialises the store. On a fresh store it used to answer nothing.

## Aggregation answers what LINQ answers (TASK-885)
The oracle is `AggregateHelper.LinqAggregate` over the documents as read back. Measured on the emulator (vnext-preview,
2026-11-10), 26 shapes, sync and async: 24 differed before, 0 after (`Task885AggregateLiveTests`).
- **Nulls are skipped.** Cosmos DB's aggregates treat a null as a value: over a group holding one, SUM and AVG were
  undefined (absent) and MIN was null, for int, decimal, double, string and DateTime members. Every aggregate argument
  is now `IS_NULL(x) ? undefined : x` (`CosmosAggregationHelper.BuildFunctionSql`, shared with the view store).
  `x ?? undefined` does not work: `??` only replaces undefined.
- **A SUM over no non-null value is 0** (TASK-886, the user's decision: one answer on every provider, as LINQ's `Sum`),
  as Cosmos DB answers it. TASK-885 had made it null with a hidden `COUNT(IS_NULL(x) ? undefined : x)`; that column is
  gone. An aggregate or group key Cosmos DB leaves undefined comes back as a null entry, so each row has every key.
- **The time bucket is applied.** It was ignored: one row where C# had five buckets. It is now grouped on
  `FLOOR(DateTimeToTimestamp(LEFT(t, 19)) / ms) * ms` and returned as `bucket_time`.
  - **LEFT 19.** In memory, a bucket floors the stored wall-clock time (`dt.Ticks`, any kind), while Cosmos DB's date
    functions convert an offset to UTC (`10:30+01:00` → `09:00Z`). So the bucket uses the first 19 characters of the
    stored text.
  - **Kind.** The bucket is `DateTimeKind.Unspecified`.
  - **Refused by name before any request:**
    - an interval that does not divide 0001-01-01 → 1970-01-01, because Cosmos DB counts from the epoch (`7 days` is
      refused; any divisor of a day passes; same rule as Elasticsearch, TASK-878);
    - an interval that is not a whole number of seconds (the fraction is not read);
    - a time column that is not `DateTime`/`DateTime?`.
  - **As in memory, `ArgumentException`:** one half of the pair, an interval that does not parse, an unknown column.
    The column is matched case-insensitively and rendered by its property name.
  - **Before 1601-01-01** (e.g. `DateTime.MinValue`), every Cosmos DB date function answers undefined. A group holding
    such a time is refused after the query, told apart from a null time by a hidden non-null count. It is never
    answered as the null bucket.
- **TASK-886 (the user's decision, 2026-11-10):** an ungrouped aggregate over no rows is one row (Count 0, Sum 0, the
  others null), as Cosmos DB answers it and every provider now does; a query with nothing to aggregate (no aggregate, no
  group, no time bucket) is refused with `ArgumentException` before any request (it was a 400, SC1001). Pinned by the
  shared `AggregateEdgeContract`.
- Result types, DateTime MIN/MAX and names: TASK-897, below.

## Aggregation answers in LINQ's types and names (TASK-897)
Oracle as above, compared strictly (same CLR type, same value). Measured on the emulator (vnext-preview, 2026-11-10),
15 shapes (12 group keys of every member type, names in other cases) x sync/async: all 15 differed; 0 after
(`Task897AggregateTypesLiveTests`).
- **Types.** Every number came back as the JSON parsed (`long` / `double`), a Guid and a DateTime as text, an enum as a
  number. Now `CosmosAggregatePlan.Read` answers the type `AggregateMath.ResultType` names (the in-memory aggregation's):
  - a group key and a MIN/MAX are read as the member is read (`JsonElement.Deserialize` with the store serializer's
    default options);
  - COUNT is an `int`; SUM/AVG (computed by Cosmos DB in double) are converted checked, so an `int` SUM past
    `int.MaxValue` throws `OverflowException` as LINQ's does;
  - **decimal:** a SUM is the double to 15 significant digits (`0.1 + 0.2` reads `0.3`; it read `0.30000000000000004`). An
    AVG is a hidden SUM and non-null COUNT divided in C# decimal (Cosmos DB's AVG read 1/3 as 0.3333333333333333). A sum
    whose exact value needs more than 15 significant digits is not exact: Cosmos DB adds in double.
- **DateTime MIN/MAX** compared the stored text, so `"…00.5Z"` sorted before `"…00Z"` (MIN of a group holding both was the
  half second). It now compares `CosmosAggregationHelper.WallClockKey`: the stored wall clock, its fraction padded to 7
  digits, then the stored suffix. It parses back to the stored value, kind included.
  - Not `DateTimeAdd` / `DateTimeToTicks`: they convert an offset to UTC, answer nothing before 1601-01-01, and the
    ticks are a double (not exact). An aggregate cannot be wrapped (`SUBSTRING(MIN(..))` is a 400), so the key is the value.
  - The order is C#'s (ticks, whatever the kind) when a stored offset is the reader's own, as the time bucket assumes.
- **A DateTime group** was one group per stored text: a local and an unspecified time with equal ticks were two groups,
  one in C#. It is now grouped on the wall clock without the suffix, and the key is the group's least `WallClockKey`.
- **Names.** Group, aggregate and time-column names are resolved as LINQ resolves them (public instance property, any
  case, its `ArgumentException`) by one lookup, `CosmosAggregationHelper.ResolveMember`, and sent as the property's name.
  The result keeps the caller's spelling. Before, `grp` read no field: every row fell into the null group, every SUM null.
- **Refused before any request:**
  - SUM/AVG of a non-numeric member, with LINQ's own `NotSupportedException` and message (`Sum is not defined for String.`);
  - MIN/MAX of a string, by name: Cosmos DB orders by code point, C# by culture (`MIN` is `"B"` where C# says `"a"`,
    measured). Also any other non-scalar or text-ordered type (`DateTimeOffset`, `TimeSpan`, `char`, objects). A Guid is
    answered: its stored lowercase hex orders as `Guid.CompareTo`;
  - a group key that is not a number, enum, bool, string, Guid or DateTime.
- **Breaking:** result types change (a caller reading `(long)row.Values["n"]` now gets an `int`); string MIN/MAX and
  non-scalar group keys throw.

## Conditional update (TASK-661)
- `AsyncCosmosDBStore.UpdateIfAsync(guid, condition, update)` is a compare-and-set on one item: read with its ETag, apply
  only where `condition` holds, replace with `IfMatchEtag`; a 412 re-reads and asks again, up to
  `MaxConditionalUpdateAttempts` (16), then `StoreConcurrencyException`. Returns the written item, or `null` when the item
  is missing or the condition fails. Refused inside a transactional batch. Async store only.

## Transaction boundary (TASK-240)

`CosmosDbUnitOfWork` wraps a `TransactionalBatch`: **atomic, but scoped to ONE logical partition key**.

- **In practice that means one entity.** `AsyncCosmosDBStore<T>` derives an item's partition key from its
  `Guid`, so **every document is its own logical partition** and a boundary spanning two entities is
  impossible by construction -- whatever the API lets you type. `Capabilities.Scope` is `SinglePartition`.
- **The limit is enforced at the call site**, not left to the server. Adding a second entity throws
  `CosmosTransactionScopeException` naming both partition keys. Previously the second `CreateItem` was
  accepted silently and the whole batch failed at `ExecuteAsync` with an opaque BadRequest -- or, if the
  caller never inspected the response, the writes were simply lost. Enforced on the whole verb family
  (create / update / upsert / delete, single and bulk), because a refused create beside an escaping delete
  is the same defect wearing a quieter coat.
- **Reads do NOT see the batch's own writes.** Operations are buffered client-side until `ExecuteAsync` and
  the batch exposes no read, so read-then-write logic inside a Cosmos boundary reads the pre-transaction
  state. `Capabilities.ReadsSeeUncommittedWrites` is `false`. This one is not fixable -- it is what a
  `TransactionalBatch` is.
- `SetTransactionContext(null)`, or a new batch, resets the pinned partition.

Pinned by `Birko.Data.CosmosDB.Tests.CosmosTransactionBoundaryTests` (7). **Deliberately not gated**: the
guard and the batch are both client-side, so a `Container` handle that never contacts a server exercises
them end to end -- gating the one assertion that matters is the failure mode this work exists to remove.
Mutation-tested: disabling the guard fails 3 of 61.

## Maintenance

### README Updates
When making changes that affect the public API, features, or usage patterns of this project, update the README.md accordingly.

### CLAUDE.md Updates
When making major changes to this project, update this CLAUDE.md to reflect new or changed components.

### Test Requirements
Every new public functionality must have corresponding unit tests. When adding new features:
- Create test classes in the corresponding test project
- Follow existing test patterns (xUnit + FluentAssertions)
- Test both success and failure cases
- Include edge cases and boundary conditions
